title: gspot.toml
description: The settings of gspot for one repository.

scope.description: Settings for one folder: its configurations and the tables that differ from the root.

format.description: Indentation, line width, quotes, and line endings for every formatter, with overrides for some paths.

limits.description: Size and complexity limits for files and functions, with values per language.

naming.description: Banned words, case, and length for the names of files, folders, and identifiers, with values per language.

cloudflare.description: The file that holds the generated Cloudflare binding types, and its interface name.

coverage.description: The lowest test coverage that the test checks accept.

dependencies.description: How many days a new release waits before an install picks it up, and the registries that lockfiles may use.

docs.description: Headings that documentation may not use, and URLs that the link check accepts.

drizzle.description: The names of Drizzle clients in your code.

javascript.description: The script files, which may print to the console and exit, and the modules the runtime provides.

python.description: The modules that the host application provides, and the folders basedpyright also searches.

trpc.description: The files that declare tRPC procedures, and the server files that other files import only as types.

zustand.description: The files that may create a Zustand store.

licenses.description: The licenses that dependencies may have, and single packages accepted with a reason.

openapi.description: The committed OpenAPI document, and the command that generates it.

postgres.description: The migrations folder, the schemas that clients read, and the migrations that may not change.

secrets.description: The env example files, and the functions in your code that read environment variables.

site.description: How the site builds, where the built files go, and the size limits of its files.

spelling.description: The language of the spelling check, such as en-us or en-gb.

supabase.description: The folders of Supabase edge functions, the schemas, and the generated types file.

translations.description: The base locale and the folder of message files.

swift.description: The Xcode project, scheme, and destination that the Swift build uses.

repository.description: The largest file that Git may track, in kilobytes.

prose.description: The longest sentence, list item, and paragraph that the prose check accepts.

duplication.description: The smallest copy, in lines and tokens, that the duplication check reports.

xcode.description: The entitlements that an Xcode project may request.

tools.description: Options for single tools, such as lint rule options. gspot writes them into the config files.

import_rule.description: Groups of files in import order: code may import the files of its own rule and of every rule listed above it.

ignore.description: Checks and lint rules turned off for some paths or everywhere, each with a reason.

command_check.description: Your own commands, run as checks with a stage, a file list, and an output format.

structure.description: Whether files may re-export the exports of other files, and which files may read environment variables.

hooks.description: Whether gspot install turns on the Git hooks.

ci.description: Whether gspot writes a CI workflow, for which provider, and on which systems it runs.

rules.description: Whether gspot writes rules for coding agents, and which rule files it leaves out.

override.reason: Migration filenames begin with their version.

reexports.reason: The library uses index files to publish its public API.

allowed_words.Acme: The project uses this product name.

__schema0.description: Correctness, security, accessibility, type safety, routine formatting, and the project's own declared checks apply at both levels. Level `all` adds checks and rules for word choice, architecture, naming, doc comments, declaration order, duplication, API style, and complexity. No level turns on experimental or preview lint rules.

__schema202.description: Your own ESLint plugins: a rule prefix as name, a tracked .js or .mjs module as path, and the rules that turn on as errors.

name.description: The rule prefix, such as local in local/no-legacy-api.

types.description: The commit types the type-enum rule allows.

scopes.description: Commit scopes that the scope-enum rule accepts, and a message may leave out its scope. When empty, gspot uses the last segment of each project scope path, or no list without project scopes.

rules.description: Options for active commitlint rules, by rule name: an always/never condition and an optional value, without a severity; the level decides which rules run. Accept a finding with gspot ignore commits/commitlint --rule `<rule>` --reason `<why>`.
Option tables for active YAML rules; the level decides which rules run, and [format] sets the width. Accept a finding with gspot ignore data-files/yamllint --rule `<rule>` --reason `<why>`.
Option tables by Markdown rule ID, such as MD024; the level decides which rules run. Accept a finding with gspot ignore markdown/markdownlint --rule `<rule>` --reason `<why>`.
Options for the Stylelint rules that run at the level, which stay errors; gspot refuses options for any other rule. Accept a finding with gspot ignore css/stylelint --rule `<rule>` --reason `<why>`.

__schema271.description: Code may import its own files and the files of every import rule listed above it, never below. can_import replaces the rules above with an exact list. When import rules exist, every code file belongs to one, apart from tests, tool settings files, scripts, and generated files.

name.description: The name that other import rules use in can_import.

paths.description: The files of the import rule.

can_import.description: Exactly the import rules whose files this rule may import, besides its own. Replaces the rules listed above it.

id.description: The check ID that `--only` and `[[ignore]] check` use, which may not match a shipped check.

stage.description: The earliest stage that runs this check.

summary.description: A short description shown in check listings.

fix.description: The executable and arguments that correct findings.

exit_codes.description: Nonzero statuses that mean findings from command and fix. Other nonzero statuses mean execution failure.

output.description: The parser and location patterns used to read findings.

format.description: How gspot reads the output: json, regex, grouped, lines, none, or the format of a named tool.

list.description: For json: the path to the list of findings.

line_base.description: Whether the tool counts lines from 0 or 1.

column.description: For json: the field that holds the column.

message.description: For json: the field that holds the message.

fixable.description: For regex: the pattern that marks a fixable finding.

message.description: For regex: the message of every finding whose pattern has no message group.
